subject: Uplift pathway: staged multi-wave term + safety-net proposal
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Stone <alicia.stone@cascade.health>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uplift pathway: staged multi-wave term + safety-net proposal

Alicia —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Attached is a concise proposal that tries to balance Cascade's desire for predictable unit economics with the flexibility to scale quickly if usage accelerates. High-level summary in the attachment, but key points below:

- Term: 24-month primary term with optional 12-month extension window tied to usage milestones (not automatic).
- Staged onramp: three scheduled uplift windows (Q1, Q3, Q9 from start) where committed capacity can step up with pre-agreed pricing bands.
- Safety-net: an overage buffer and a one-time true-up credit if actual monthly peak exceeds staged capacity by more than 40% in two consecutive months.
- Auto-renew: default auto-renew only for the primary 24-month term unless Cascade opts out 60 days before renewal; extension window requires affirmative sign-off.
- Co-alignment: synchronize billing boundary to Cascade's fiscal Q1 to minimize mid-year true-ups (we can co-term to your fiscal calendar).

Operational asks on our side (in short): production forecast for first 6 months by Oct 12, list of restricted models for compliance review, and a point of contact for procurement. I copied Jonas to loop in ops and implementation early.

I'll plan a short 30-min alignment call next week to walk the proposal if that works — available Wed/Thu morning PT.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Naomi —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clean summary. A few clarifying questions before we loop legal/procurement:

1) Can you make the extension window opt-in (we prefer affirmative opt-in rather than any implicit extension)?
2) For the safety-net true-up credit: what does the reconciliation look like operationally? How soon would we see a credit applied?
3) We need an option to lock the pricing bands for the first 12 months irrespective of usage upswing — our CFO will push back on open-ended price exposure in year 1.

Procurement (cc) is copied — can you confirm whether Redwood provides a single master SOW with staggered schedules, or do you prefer individual amendment attachments for each staged uplift? Also please include any SOC2 evidence references in the next send.

Alicia Stone
Head of Data Platforms

Alicia / Naomi —

Quick follow from the ops/implementation side. Naomi, feel free to forward to procurement. Alicia, answers inline: 

1) Extension window opt-in: yes — we can change the language to require affirmative execution of the 12-month extension SOW at least 45 days before the end of the primary term. That satisfies opt-in and gives both sides time to lock pricing.

2) Safety-net reconciliation: operational flow we recommend:
   - We run daily issuance metrics and a monthly peak report (monthly close within 5 business days).
   - If a qualifying two-month exceedance is detected, Redwood issues a one-time invoice credit within the following invoice cycle (usually net 30 from detection).
   - We can include a protective clause capping total annual credits to the value of one staged uplift to avoid unbounded exposure.

3) Price lock for year 1: we can commit to locked unit rates on the baseline and first staged uplift for months 1–12. Subsequent uplift windows revert to the pre-agreed pricing bands unless both parties agree otherwise.

Operational items we need from Cascade to finalize the SOW and implementation timeline:
- Forecast (CSV) for months 1–6 (send by Oct 12)
- List of models that will be restricted to on-prem/private deployment (for compliance/legal review)
- Confirmation whether Cascade requires invoice cadence to follow calendar months or fiscal periods (we can co-term to fiscal).

I'm attaching a short ops checklist that we usually include with multi-wave renewals — it maps dates to milestones and owners. Naomi: can you share this with procurement?

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Principal Implementation Manager
Redwood Inference
